explanation: Clinical stages of Hodgkin Lymphoma (Ann Arbor classification). Stage I= Involvement of a single lymph node region or extralymphatic site. Stage II= Involvement of two or more lymph node region or an extralymphatic site and lymph node regions on the same side of (above or below) the diaphragm. Stage III= Involvement of lymph node regions on both sides of the diaphragm with or without localized extralymphatic involvement of the spleen or both. question: A female present with menorrhagia and mucosal bleeding. Laboratory investigations show: increased bleeding time (BT), normal PT and APTT, and markedly decreased von Willebrand factor (vWF) levels. Which of the following processes is primarily affected?
explanation: The primary function of von Willebrand factor (vWF) is in platelet adhesion: Platelet Adhesion: This is the first step in forming a platelet plug, where platelets stick to the damaged blood vessel wall. vWF mediates this initial sticking. Therefore, low vWF directly impairs adhesion, leading to a prolonged bleeding time (BT). Platelet Aggregation: This is the second step, where platelets stick to other platelets to build up the plug. This is primarily mediated by Fibrinogen binding to the platelet GPIIb/IIIa receptor, not vWF.
